- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.25) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25), model often overcorrects downward; avoid sharp downward revisions; consider slight upward bias.
- Model frequently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon, especially after recent highs; apply downward bias for first 5–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >5% above 14-day moving average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.25) and price is trending, model often fails to capture momentum; adjust forecast to align with recent 7-day average.
- Forecast should not exceed 3–5% above the 18-day moving average unless sentiment strongly supports it.
